scope: Rust/Metal folder create/rename, folder deletion/save-error and workspace deletion modal actions and Rust outer-body allocation. Shared scene client retains native bubble frame, focus/AX/scroll/input-protection adapters. Page and migrated modal widgets/delegates are explicitly client owned.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.

Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

contracts: Rust folder create/rename, folder deletion/save-error and workspace deletion no longer construct DialogModel/BubbleDialogModelHost or native MdTextButton/Label action controls. The existing Rust form/notice state and body scenes, existing native domain callbacks and shared Rust/Metal action controls are retained. Views mode keeps its original model-host baseline.

SceneModalDialog retains the native BubbleDialogDelegate window/frame, autosizing, theme and rounded client-layer policy. Rust panel layout allocates its single body with original native side insets and 2px scroll-content margin. Native ScrollView retains the original maximum-height cap, disabled horizontal scrolling and top/bottom control/text margins. Modal fixed width and button order/metrics remain native inputs to Rust placement.

The shared SceneDialogClient owns action nodes and row layout without invoking the private native-button allocator. Native default focus, Return/Escape, enabled/default AX metadata, input protection and once-only native Accept/Cancel remain. Its fixed-width minimum avoids adding the action row twice. Empty action rows have zero natural size; default accelerators are removed when a control stops being the default. Model-row replacement never leaves its stored row pointer empty during hierarchy notifications.

All migrated modal delegates are owned by the application and destroyed after their CLIENT_OWNS_WIDGET widgets. Folder widgets now close synchronously and invalidate editors/canvases immediately; folder weak handles remain the existing API. Detach destroys widgets before delegates. PageDialogs also now retains its delegate directly instead of releasing an unowned delegate through the legacy unique_ptr widget helper. The previous native comparison fixture likewise owns its plain delegate explicitly.

The shared browser case compares original BubbleDialogModelHost preferred/minimum client size, margins, fixed width and body rectangles against the Rust wrapper using the same measured body, for folder editing, folder deletion and workspace deletion. It verifies childless Metal actions, AX/default metadata and real Cocoa Space/Return/Escape cancellation/creation. A dedicated Metal case closes three composing editors with CloseNow, checks client weak lifetimes, acknowledges a one-button save error, reopens a clean editor and destroys it on shell Detach. The one-button error is acknowledged with actual Cocoa Return after successful presentation.

Existing form/notice validation, empty/overlong names, IME admission, captured targets, stale workspace/folder errors, beforeunload, profile retention, screen bounds, page-dialog/default-key and shared chrome cases remain in critical/full regression coverage. No browser-service callback, validation/authorization rule, persisted store or dependency was changed.

Native title/frame, scroll/window/event/focus/AX containers, other forms/service panels and remaining native ownership still require migration or explicit platform-adapter acceptance. This does not complete Views removal or establish CPU/GPU/presentation or memory improvements.

retained_first_probe.reason: Actual Cocoa Escape did not close the textless folder-delete modal on either backend. Body metrics and default Cancel Return checks were preserved. The shared failing test is byte-identical in final code. Production routing now dispatches registered dialog accelerators for folder deletion/save errors and workspace notices in both backends.
